topic: Security basics: 5 things every app should have from day one
caption:
Security isn't a feature you add later. These 5 basics belong in version one. 🔐

1️⃣ HTTPS everywhere
2️⃣ Passwords hashed, never stored
3️⃣ Secrets out of the code
4️⃣ The right access for the right user
5️⃣ Updates and backups

None of these are expensive on day one. All of them are expensive to fix after a breach. Swipe for the why. →

slides.title: 5 things every app needs from day one.
slides.sub: Cheap to build in. Expensive to fix after a breach.

slides.title: HTTPS everywhere
slides.body: Every request between your app and server should be encrypted in transit. No exceptions, including admin panels and APIs.

slides.title: Hash every password
slides.body: Use a proven hashing algorithm or a managed auth service. If your database leaks, passwords shouldn't.

slides.title: Keep secrets out of the code
slides.body: API keys and database passwords belong in environment variables or a secrets manager, not in your repo.

slides.title: Right access, right user
slides.body: Check permissions on the server, not just in the UI. Users should only ever see their own data.

slides.title: Updates and backups
slides.body: Patch dependencies regularly and run automated backups you've actually tested restoring.
